Patient has lower abdominal pain.

Abdominal pain comes and goes.
Abdominal pain does not radiate to the back.
Patient feels weak.
Patient feels shaky.
No blood in stools observed.
Patient vomited at the start of the symptoms.
Vomiting has stopped.
No blood in vomit reported.
Patient has loss of appetite.
Patient has been able to hold down fluids.
Patient has been eating soups.
Patient has been eating light foods like smoothies.
Patient felt hot when symptoms started about three to four days ago.
Patient has no fever at present.
Patient ate takeaway about four days ago.
Patient ate at a Chinese restaurant.
No family members have the same symptoms.
One child vomited without diarrhea.
Patient needs to stay close to the toilet due to frequent diarrhea.
Symptoms have affected the patient's day-to-day activities.

Patient has asthma.

Patient reports no other tummy or bowel problems.
Patient takes no other medications.

Patient does not smoke.

Clinician suspects gastroenteritis.
Antibiotics were not recommended.
Patient was advised to maintain hydration.
Oral rehydration solution such as Dioralyte was recommended.

Patient was advised to take two to three days off work to rest.
Patient was advised to seek review if symptoms do not improve in three to four days.
Stool sample testing may be needed if symptoms are ongoing.
